trigger_condition: The new handler's response body contract (ProblemDetail title, generic detail, empty schemaValidationErrors) is never asserted; the tests only check the 400 status.
guard_snippet: In VisitRestControllerV1Tests.testCreateVisitError (or PetRestControllerV1Tests.testUpdatePetNullNameReturns400), add .andExpect(jsonPath("$.title").value("HttpMessageNotReadableException")).andExpect(jsonPath("$.detail").value("The request contains invalid or missing parameters")) and assert the body does not contain the record constructor message (e.g. "description must be between").
potential_consequence: If someone changes the handler's detail to e.getMessage() or e.getCause().getMessage(), the record constructor and Jackson internals leak to clients. Every added test (testCreateVisitError, testCreateVisitEmptyDescriptionReturns400, testCreateVisitNegativePetIdReturns400, testUpdatePetNullNameReturns400, testUpdatePetTooLongNameReturns400) ends at status().isBadRequest(), so none would fail. The sibling MethodArgumentNotValid and 500 paths do have body assertions (OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.java:397-403, 465-467), so this path is the exception.
consumer: Clients of POST /api/visits, PUT /api/visits/{id} and PUT /api/pets/{id}, whose bodies are now rejected by the PetDto and VisitDto compact constructors and reach this handler; also every other endpoint, where malformed JSON now returns 400 instead of the 500 from the catch-all handler.
evidence: Read the full diff and ExceptionControllerAdvice.java:40-150. Grepped src for HttpMessageNotReadable: it appears only in the advice, with no test reference. Grepped jsonPath in the Owner, Pet and Visit V1 controller tests: the Visit and Pet 400 tests added in this diff (VisitRestControllerV1Tests.java:175-199 and 223-228, PetRestControllerV1Tests.java:172-212) assert only status().isBadRequest(). The jsonPath title and detail assertions in OwnerRestControllerV1Tests cover only MethodArgumentNotValidException and the 500 handler.
